jobs.title: Project Management Intern at Fessler & Bowman, Inc.
jobs.description: Employer: Fessler & Bowman, Inc. Expires: 09/14/2026 Founded in 1963 by Don Fessler & George Bowman, Fessler & Bowman, Inc. has grown from a residential flatwork & basement wall contractor to a top 100 Commercial Concrete Contractor recognized across the nation. Keeping customer satisfaction as our fundamental core value has allowed Fessler & Bowman, Inc. to prosper for nearly six decades. Our Culture & Philosophy:Fessler & Bowman is a fast-paced and culture-focused industry leader in specialty concrete and civil earthwork. When we talk about culture at F&B, it is not just a plaque hanging in our lobby. Our values are our driving force and have allowed us to build a phenomenal team delivering best in class products to our customers. Open & ConstructiveTake Pride in Our ProductRelentless CommitmentCare About Our CustomersTeam Success Summary:The Project Management Team is responsible for the successful completion of construction projects, from the initial hand-off from Estimating through final completion and close-out. PMs are responsible for overall project planning and scheduling, resource allocation, project accounting, and control, while providing technical direction and ensuring compliance with quality standards and applicable laws and regulations. As a Project Management Intern, you will assist in all of these activities by offering support and utilizing prior knowledge. The descriptions below are representative of, but not limited to, the expectations of this role. Five Key Roles of the Project Management Intern:Organizing and planning for the safe and efficient execution of the assigned projectsAssist in maintaining the financial controls of the project for the profit/loss of the projectAssisting in developing and maintaining the project scheduleCollaborating with PM team to estimate, price and negotiate the price on projectsWorking with Superintendents and Estimating teams for project collaboration Essential Duties & Responsibilities:Assisting with department initiativesContinually expanding knowledge and use of industry best practices and innovationSolving problems, as they arise, by using available knowledge and resourcesOther duties as assigned Education, Experience & Qualifications:Currently working towards a degree in Construction Management or related fieldCompetency with computers and basic programs/softwareExcellent written and oral communication skillsDetail-oriented and excellent organization skillsCreative and results-oriented, with a strong sense of urgency and self-motivationExcellent problem-solving skills, with an adaptable and flexible style in working with all types of individuals Travel:Light travel may be required for this position. Travel may include, but is not limited to, travel from office to various job sites. Fessler and Bowman will compensate for travel when applicable. Work Environment:As a Project Management Intern, you will be subject to various work environments. Environments include but are not limited to the following: office and field settings, high/low temperatures, areas close to traffic, loud and frequent noises, confined spaces, heights, indoor/outdoor settings. Recruitment Process:The recruitment process will include a phone screen, in-person meeting, and a pre-employment background check and drug test. Fessler & Bowman is an Equal Opportunity Employer

jobs.title: Designer at Moglea
jobs.description: Employer: Moglea Expires: 09/14/2026 Position: Designer 8/14/26IN-PERSON POSITION - Part - Time - 20 hours weeklyWe're seeking a part-time Designer to join our Design Team. The Design Team is responsible for various creative aspects of the Moglea brand. Applicants should have a design-focused educational background with knowledge of programs like Photoshop, InDesign, and Illustrator. Experience with video and social media is a plus. Responsibilities include but are not limited to, designing engaging email campaigns, editing images, assisting in planning and producing social media content, and shooting video footage. Our Design Team also assists our creative directors with designing new products for the Moglea line. Our Design Team also plans and coordinates marketing efforts for the brand. We’re looking for someone who is organized, flexible, and ready to bring fresh ideas to the Moglea brand.Our Company: Moglea was launched in 2012 and is under the creative direction of Chad and Meg Gleason. Their artful stationery and product line is created by using hand-applied production processes to add one-of-a-kind elements to each product. The production team in their Des Moines, Iowa-based studio thoughtfully applies layers of paint to extra-thick sheets of paper before cutting them down, yielding completely unique compositions. Each piece is finished on one of their antique presses where it is foil stamped, printed, or die-cut using traditional letterpress printing processes. The Moglea line is a joyful exploration of composition, pattern and color. For each new release, Chad and Meg intentionally focus on adding unexpected production processes or visual ideas to the current collection. The result is a product line in which each piece feels like a work of art that is meant to be shared. The Moglea line is sold worldwide, with placement in over 1000 stores. The line has been sold nationwide by retailers such as Anthropologie, West Elm, CB2, Nordstrom, and Blick Art Materials. Our ValuesSincerity: We speak honestly and from our heart. We believe in caring personally and challenging directly as a means to improve performance when working together. We share our own stories and extend space for others to share theirs. We truly think this is the best and only way we can continue to grow as a team and company. Accountability: We embrace mistakes and learn together. We listen, observe, and gather information that brings us closer to understanding our team. We take responsibility for mistakes and create solutions for how to improve. Respect: We respect and listen to all members of our team, whether new to Moglea or senior employees. We respect and value the mission of the Moglea organization and the decisions our founders make toward that vision. Empathy: We desire to truly know and understand all members of our team - their points of view, their motivations, and their personal feelings. We desire to match our team’s strengths and skills to roles that can make the most impact. Our understanding of others will help build sustainable and productive relationships that help improve the corporate intimacy within the culture at Moglea. Humility: We recognize that we can, and we will be wrong. New information, time, and new levels of understanding ask us to challenge our previously held opinions and seek to improve ourselves and our work. We will be open to feedback from our peers, those above us, and our direct reports. We will self-reflect on recent decisions and motivations. Adaptive Tenacity: We passionately commit to our goals and stick to that commitment with a spirit of open-hearted and earnest striving and life-long learning. We are growth-minded and ask that all employees continue to grow and adapt to the growth of our company. We seek to accomplish higher performance levels, improved communication, and stronger relationships with all Moglea employees. Integrity: We ask that all Moglea employees are trustworthy, do what is right, and lead by example. Ownership: We don’t wait for others to act. We take the initiative to bring about positive results. We ask that employees care about Moglea products, processes, property, and personnel just as much as an owner of the company would. Taking ownership means we are accountable for the results of our actions and that they are executed with the highest quality and in a timely manner. Joy: We acknowledge that as coworkers, we see each other more than family and friends. Work can be challenging but overall should be fun, joyful, and fulfilling to every member of the Moglea team. We seek to ensure that every employee has a net positive experience while working at Moglea. Primary duties:• Maintaining the aesthetic quality of the Moglea brand. • Designing work such as email campaigns and social media content. • Plan and execute sales and marketing campaigns. • Collect market research, identifying potential markets and testing. • Editing and preparing images for use across various platforms. • Updating shop and social media platforms with fresh content. • Shooting and editing video footage of the production team. • Assisting the Design Team with other tasks as assigned. • Planning and brainstorming new ideas for video content. • Designing brand collateral for the Moglea brand. • Developing new color palettes and mood boards for each collection. • Designing brand collateral for the Moglea Furniture line. • Developing new production processes and assisting with process execution within the studio. • Assisting with production as needed for large orders or during busy times. • Stocking and merchandising the DSM retail shop. • Assisting with events within the retail shop. • Assisting customers within the retail shop. • (potential / growth in role) - Designing products and packaging for Moglea Paper line.Desired Education/Experience/SkillsAdobe Suite, especially Illustrator, Photoshop, InDesign and Premier Pro. Instagram / Social media. Experience with shooting and editing video is required. Must have the ability to use basic video editing apps like CapCut, Edits and Premier Pro. Position Type: Part-time. In Person. Starting Pay Range: The pay range will be from 40-45K annual base salary with benefits. The pay range will be $ 20- $ 26 per hour for part-time positions. Our full-time Design positions are salary positions with benefits (HRA, retirement savings, paid vacation and sick days, employee discount, free downtown parking spot, Friday happy hour, Staff Lunches.) Our initial package is 10 paid days, 7 paid holidays, 3 paid sick days, and 10 days of parental leave. lBenefits:• Flexible schedule - We can accommodate any schedule between 6 AM-7 PM, Monday through Friday. • Free cards. • Relaxed work environment. • Ability to learn and grow within a creative environment. Location:Our production studio is downtown Des Moines at 110 11th Street, Des Moines, IA 50309. Equal Opportunity Employer: We are an equal employment opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability status, protected veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law. Application Process:Please email jobs@moglea.com and submit:Your cover letter, resume (if you have one or just a listing of job history if applicable), and a portfolio link or PDF. Your cover letter should state why you think you would be a great fit at Moglea or why you would like to work at Moglea. Please also put the position you are applying for in the subject line of your email - DesignerWe appreciate you taking the time to consider yourself for this position. If you have any questions, please email jobs@moglea.com.

jobs.title: Visual Design Intern at The Autoimmune Fund
jobs.description: Employer: The Autoimmune Fund Expires: 09/14/2026 More than 100 autoimmune diseases affect tens of millions of Americans, yet the field is still difficult to see as a connected ecosystem. The Autoimmune Fund is building a new way to understand the autoimmune patient journey, and to invest across it. We use visual communication to make that complexity understandable.We are looking for a design intern to help us build one of the foundations of that system: a reusable icon library and visual grammar for The Autoimmune Fund.To ApplySend the following to bonnie@autoimmune.fund.Your resume. A short PDF or a link is fine.A few sentences about why this project interests you.One example of a visual system you designed yourself. A set of related marks or icons built according to shared rules, rather than a single icon or logo. Include a short explanation of the thinking or rules behind it.A quick visual-thinking challenge. Choose one of these three ideas: Immune Precision, convergence, or investment conviction. Show us in a rough sketch, or in a few sentences, how you might represent it visually and why.Section 1 · The ProjectThis is not an assignment to draw a collection of unrelated icons. It is a visual systems and information-design project.You will work with our existing storyboards, presentations, one-pagers and reports to identify the concepts we communicate repeatedly, from patients, diagnostics and capital to more abstract ideas such as immune precision, convergence and investment conviction.Some concepts have familiar visual shorthand. Others do not. For the hardest ones, we want you to explore the question:What is the simplest, most intelligent visual expression of this idea?Your goal will be to turn these concepts into a coherent visual vocabulary that can work across presentations, reports and digital materials, and that can be extended by other designers without losing its consistency.Section 2 · What You Will Build1. Visual Audit and VocabularyIdentify recurring concepts, symbols and visual inconsistencies.Build a master visual-vocabulary taxonomy.Group concepts into families such as patient journey, science, technology, healthcare, markets and investing.Determine which concepts need icons, proprietary symbols, visual metaphors, connectors or other reusable components.Prioritize the concepts we use most frequently.Deliverable: Master visual vocabulary and prioritized icon inventory.2. Visual Metaphor ExplorationExplore multiple visual approaches for approximately 8 to 12 core concepts, including proprietary Autoimmune Fund frameworks.Develop different metaphors and abstractions before moving to a finished icon.Recommend the visual directions that make unfamiliar ideas easiest to understand.Deliverable: Visual metaphor studies and recommended directions.3. Visual GrammarHelp establish rules for line weight, geometry, scale and proportion, level of detail, spacing and optical alignment, containers and shapes, color usage, and filled versus outline treatments.Develop arrows, pathways, gates, brackets, flows and other connectors that allow individual symbols to tell larger stories.Deliverable: Icon and visual-grammar standards.4. Core Icon LibraryCreate and refine approximately 30 to 40 high-priority icons covering the concepts we use most often.Use or adapt familiar universal symbols where they work. Reserve original visual solutions for concepts that need them.Deliverable: Core Autoimmune Fund icon library.5. Proprietary Visual LanguageDevelop a smaller family of distinctive symbols for recurring Autoimmune Fund scientific frameworks and investment concepts.Keep them simple enough to work alongside the broader icon library, but distinctive enough to become recognizable across our materials.Deliverable: Approximately 8 to 10 proprietary symbols.6. Working Figma LibraryBuild organized Figma components with naming conventions, categories and appropriate variants.Incorporate connectors and visual-grammar elements.Prepare SVG and presentation-ready assets, and test the system at real presentation and document sizes.Document basic usage rules so the library can grow without losing consistency.Deliverable: An organized, extensible visual communication library.Section 3 · Who We Are Looking ForYou may be studying graphic design, communication design, information design, visual communication or a closely related field. We are looking for someone who:Thinks in systems rather than individual graphics.Is excellent at reducing complicated ideas to simple visual forms.Understands what makes an icon family feel consistent.Has strong composition and information-design instincts.Is fluent in Figma and comfortable creating clean vector artwork.Can explore several visual solutions before becoming attached to one.Notices details but understands that clarity matters more than decoration.Can explain why a visual solution works.You do not need a background in venture capital, investing or immunology. We will provide the science, strategy, source material and regular art direction.You bring visual intelligence, curiosity and craft.Section 4 · What This Is NotThis is not primarily character illustration, branding or logo design, UX/UI product design, or production work using downloaded icon packs. We are looking for someone interested in visual meaning, information design and systems thinking.Section 5 · What You Will Leave WithRather than a series of disconnected intern assignments, you will have the opportunity to build a complete visual system that can become a substantial portfolio case study.Complex problem → research → visual exploration → design rules → icon system → working component library → real-world applicationSection 6 · Project StructureCommitment: Part-time, approximately 10 to 12 hours per weekInitial project: Approximately 20 hoursEstimated full project: Approximately 60 to 80 hoursCompensation: $20 per hourLocation: Los Angeles or UCLA-area availability is a plus. We will consider an exceptional remote candidate.The initial project will focus on the visual audit, taxonomy and early metaphor exploration. The internship may then continue into development of the full library, based on mutual fit and the strength of the initial work.

jobs.description: Employer: Southern Hospitality Internship Program (SHIP) Expires: 09/16/2026 THE ROLEGreat Big Game Show Hosts are world-class hospitality experts who genuinely love people, thrive in high-energy environments, and take pride in creating unforgettable guest experiences.As a Host, you’ll lead guests through our live, hour-long game show experiences, where teams compete in 8-10 fast-paced mini-games involving physical challenges, trivia, luck, and skill. Through direct work with families, engaging technical assistance partnerships, and by advocating for policies that drive systemic change, we’re fighting poverty by lifting two generations at once. Our team culture is rooted in deep respect for the parents we partner with and for each other. We’re looking for dedicated team members who share our vision that, 25 years from now, LIFT is no longer needed because we have helped build a social service system grounded in Hope, Money, and Love, where all families can thrive. We’re guided by mission- and strategy-aligned leadership grounded in kindness, curiosity, relationships, and a commitment to equity. This position may be done remotely from any state where LIFT currently operates.POSITION OVERVIEW This is a part-time internship requiring approximately 20 hours per month through December 31, 2026, with the possibility of extension. This role will report to the Director, Individual Giving, and will work closely with the Communications Manager. This part-time Development & Communications intern will support LIFT’s fundraising-focused communications efforts and external-facing communications. The internship is writing-driven, with responsibility for developing donor-facing communications, social media, and organizational content, creating compelling stories and content that engage supporters, strengthen relationships, advance fundraising goals, and broaden LIFT's reach and visibility.AS THE DEVELOPMENT & COMMUNICATION INTERN YOU WILL… DevelopmentDraft and edit donor-facing communications and development content that engage supporters, communicate impact, and strengthen relationships with donors and partners. Create and refine templates and adaptable content that can be used across multiple cities, ensuring consistency while tailoring messaging for local contexts.Support the development and execution of fundraising-focused communications strategies that effectively engage and retain donors.Develop clear, concise, and compelling written content that reflects both local impact and a broader national perspective.Collaborate with internal stakeholders to gather input and ensure alignment on messaging, while working independently.Proofread and edit content with a high level of attention to detail, ensuring accuracy, clarity, and consistency in tone and branding across materials.Explore opportunities to enhance communication through visual storytelling, including basic graphic design and video content to support fundraising efforts.Support broader development and communications activities, including event preparation, coordination, and administrative support as neededCommunicationsManage LIFT's social media presence day-to-day — writing and building posts, maintaining a consistent content calendar, and adapting content across platforms.Support the writing and editing of external content including the monthly newsletter, blog posts, and the annual report.Copy edit across external materials, serving as a reliable second pair of eyes on accuracy, consistency, tone, and brand.Track relevant news, research, and field conversations to surface content opportunities.OUR IDEAL CANDIDATE Strong writing and editing skills, with the ability to produce clear, concise, and compelling content for a range of audiences, including donors, partners, and social media audiences.Experience or interest in development and fundraising communications, donor engagement, and mission-driven storytelling.Fluency with social media as a communications tool. Comfortable writing copy and creating content for LinkedIn, Instagram, X, and Facebook, and maintaining a content calendar.Ability to work independently in a remote, flexible environment.High attention to detail, including proofreading for accuracy, consistency, and grammatical correctness.Self-motivated with a willingness to learn and grow skills in areas such as fundraising strategy, graphic design, and multimedia content (e.g., video).Strong organizational skills and attention to detail, with the ability to contribute to longer-term projects by managing timelines, tracking tasks, and meeting deadlines.LIFT’S COMPETENCIESAll LIFT employees embrace and demonstrate our organization-wide core competencies:Communication: You share information with relevant parties in a clear and timely manner; effectively engage with and present to others; and write and verbally communicate in a manner that conveys understanding of relevant information and issues.Accountability: You take responsibility for the quality and timeliness of work and achieve results with appropriate levels of oversight. You receive feedback in a constructive manner.Inclusiveness: You help create a work environment that appreciates diversity and encourages equity by treating others with respect, listening to, and demonstrating appreciation for others’ perspectives, and using culturally sensitive language.Teamwork: You work effectively with others throughout the organization and promote cooperation and commitment within your team to achieve goals and deliverables.Results-orientation: You focus on results and desired outcomes, keeping team and organizational goals in mind. You use sound planning to achieve goals and get the job done.Problem-solving: You take the initiative to solve problems. You exhibit resourcefulness, innovation, and adaptability to new situations.Don’t think you have everything for this role but are still interested? Please don’t hesitate to apply. We’d love to hear from you! LIFT is an equal opportunity employer and believes that diversity in all dimensions of the organization supports and bolsters the innovative thinking essential to its success and is committed to providing equal employment opportunity to all qualified applicants. LIFT’s goal is for our people to reflect the communities in which we live and serve and to ensure representation of people of color, those who identify as women, veterans, and individuals with disabilities in our organization. WHAT WE OFFER Hourly rate: $22/hour. LIFT’s compensation philosophy is to pay competitively for our non-profit sector and ensure equity across the organization. The compensation range we offer represents a good faith estimate of what we may pay for the position at the time of posting. To ensure we meet our equity and inclusion standards, where a candidate is placed in the range will be assessed based on the market for the position, their qualifications, internal equity, and budget. jobs.title: Strategic Marketing Intern at TADA Mobility (USA) LLC
jobs.description: Employer: TADA Mobility (USA) LLC Expires: 09/19/2026 About ThrooThroo is a Singapore-based ride-hailing platform that has disrupted the Southeast Asian market since its launch in 2018. Unlike traditional giants like Uber or Lyft, Throo operates on a zero-commission model. Instead of taking a large percentage of every fare (often 20% or more), Throo charges drivers a small, fixed platform fee. This ensures that drivers retain more of their hard-earned income and riders enjoy more competitive, transparent pricing.Powered by MVL’s blockchain, Throo creates a "fairness-first" ecosystem. By recording ride data securely and transparently, the platform incentivizes safe driving and high service quality through a token-based rewards system. Having already captured significant market share in Singapore, Cambodia, Vietnam, Thailand, and Hong Kong, Throo is now bringing its blockchain-backed, driver-centric model to the West, with New York City serving as the cornerstone of its North American expansion.About the RoleThroo is expanding, and we are looking for a Strategic Marketing Intern to join our foundational New York City Launch Team. NYC is the most competitive and regulated ride-hailing market globally. We need a high-velocity, intellectually curious individual to help build Throo’s brand from the ground up in New York City.You will work directly with the Launch Lead to create UGC content, design a localized messaging strategy, and execute the marketing playbook that will define Throo’s success in North America.Key Responsibilities1. NYC Market Entry & Messaging StrategyHyper-Local Messaging: Craft the "Why Throo" narrative specifically for the NYC market, differentiating us from incumbents (Uber/Lyft/Revel) for both driver-partners and riders.Segmented Campaigns: Develop bespoke messaging strategies for diverse NYC segments—from Manhattan commuters to outer-borough driver communities.GTM Execution: Support the end-to-end execution of the New York Go-To-Market (GTM) strategy across digital, OOH (Out-of-Home), and grassroots channels.Content Creation: Create UGC or other marketing materials to onboard New Yorkers2. Stakeholder Mapping & AdvocacyInfluence Mapping: Identify and map key NYC power players, including TLC (Taxi & Limousine Commission) influencers, driver unions/guilds, and local community leaders.Partnership Scoping: Identify and vet local NYC brand partners (lifestyle, fintech, or events) for co-marketing opportunities that provide immediate "street cred" and user trust.Public Perception: Assist in managing PR efforts to position Throo as the "fairer" alternative in the NYC transport ecosystem.What You’ll NeedNYC DNA: Deep familiarity with the New York City landscape, culture, and transit habits.Creativity Mindset: Positive, experimental approach to content creationStrategic Rigor: Ability to map complex stakeholder ecosystems and translate "fairness" into a compelling, high-conversion marketing hook.Communication: "First-class" written and verbal skills; ability to hold your own in a room with senior leadership and external partners.Why This Role?Zero-to-One Experience: You aren't maintaining a brand; you are building one in the world's most famous city.High Visibility: As part of a lean launch team, your work on messaging and stakeholder mapping will be seen and used by Throo’s global leadership.Impact: Direct involvement in one of the most significant milestones in Throo’s company history.

jobs.title: Program Manager Premier College Intern Program at WPAFB Program Manager Trainee Program
jobs.description: Employer: WPAFB Program Manager Trainee Program Expires: 09/20/2026 About WPAFB Program Manager Trainee ProgramLooking for Civilian Program Managers to lead the Air Force into the 21st centuryOne of six centers under Air Force Materiel Command, the Air Force Life Cycle Management Center is the single center responsible for total life cycle management of Air Force weapon systems.The AFLCMC Mission: "Acquire and Support War-Winning Capabilities"Our Motto: "AFLCMC...Providing the Warfighter's Edge"We are currently recruiting Sophomore or Junior students to come work for the U.S. Air Force at Wright-Patterson AFB as a Program Manager in the Premier College Intern Program for the summer of 2027. What is a Program Manager (PM)? What does a Program Manager do in the Air Force?An Acquisition Program Manager leads a team of multi-functional professionals in the acquisition and support of Air Force weapon systems: aircraft, weapons, training systems, IT and business systems at the Air Force Life Cycle Management Center (AFLCMC). As an Air Force program manager you will be responsible for managing and coordinating all aspects of an acquisition program to achieve the cost, schedule, performance and sustainment goals of your customers, the men and women who fly, operate, or maintain this country’s most advanced aircraft and systems. Your primary role will be that of the team leader. You will be "the buck stops here" individual who must be able to solve problems and make decisions by leading and motivating a diverse group of individuals to perform as a cohesive and effective team. The acquisition program manager must have organizational and people skills, communication skills, and analytical skills. Additionally, as the leader of a multi-functional team, the program manager must be familiar with the roles and responsibilities of the other team members (logistics managers, financial managers, engineers and contracting specialists, etc.) Experienced, senior program managers often manage an entire aircraft program, like the F-22 Raptor. But as a new program manager, you will more often be responsible for a piece of a major program, like the modification of an item that is integral to an aircraft. Your responsibilities will grow rapidly as you gain experience and demonstrate the ability to handle more complex acquisition programs.These are full time (40 hour/week) positions at Wright-Patterson Air Force Base for 10 to 12 weeks over the summer of 2027. After successful completion of the PM Summer Intern Program, the individual is offered a full-time PM position to start as a GS-07 upon successful completion of a bachelors degree. Pay is set by number of course hours complete at the start of the internship. If 60 or more course hours, you will be paid at the GS-04 level. If more than 120 course hours complete, you will be paid at the GS-05 level. What we need from you:- If interested in this position please send me your updated resume and transcripts to devon.aey@us.af.mil. After verifying eligibility, I will reach out to you to set up an interview. Questions:- If you have any questions at all, please feel free to contact the USAF POC Devon Aey at devon.aey@us.af.mil. He is ready and willing to address any questions you may have or discuss more about the Job or the Program. Don’t hesitate to email.

jobs.title: Forward Deployment Engineer at AppleOne Employment Services
jobs.description: Employer: AppleOne Employment Services Expires: 09/20/2026 About ActOne GroupActOne Group Industries builds and deploys AI agents and automations that run real business workflows for enterprise clients. Our platform, Foundry, lets teams design, build, and ship AI applications and agents — and we work side-by-side with clients to get those solutions into production. We're a small, fast-moving team where the work you do reaches customers quickly. About the RoleThis is a Forward Deployment Engineer (FDE) internship — but you don't need a traditional engineering background. You need sharp business instincts, genuine curiosity about AI, and the drive to learn how to build.Forward Deployment Engineers sit at the intersection of client and product. You'll learn how to translate a client's business problems into working AI agents and applications, build them on Foundry using Claude Code, and help clients do the same. A big part of the summer is helping us design and build a client training program — alongside our AI Lead — that teaches customers how to build their own AI applications and agents from scratch.If you've been the person who picks up new tools fast, builds things on the side, and likes being in the room with customers, this is for you. Why This Is an Exciting OpportunityThe way work gets done is being rewritten right now, and Forward Deployment Engineers are the people doing the rewriting. You won't be watching the AI shift from the sidelines — you'll be on the front line of it, sitting with real businesses and turning "what if AI could do this?" into something that's actually running in production.This is a rare chance to get genuinely fluent in the tools and workflows that will define the next decade of work, while you're still early. You'll build real AI agents and applications, shape how clients learn to build their own, and develop a skill set very few people have yet: knowing how to take AI from a demo to deployed value. The people who learn this now — how to think with these tools, sell with them, and ship with them — are the ones who will be leading teams and companies in a few years. We're betting that's you. What You'll DoWork directly with clients to understand their workflows, goals, and where AI can create real valueLearn to build AI agents and applications on the Foundry platform using Claude CodeHelp design and build our client-facing training program alongside the AI Lead — the curriculum that teaches clients how to build and deploy their own AI solutionsSupport client onboarding and the hands-on deployment of solutionsGet deep, practical exposure to the leading AI tools — Claude, OpenAI, and the broader stack — and develop strong judgment about when and how to use eachDocument patterns, write clear guides, and turn what works into repeatable playbooks Who You AreStrong business fundamentals — you understand how companies actually operate and make decisionsHands-on AI exposure — you've used tools like Claude and OpenAI extensively, ideally building real things with them, not just experimentingA fast, self-directed learner — comfortable with ambiguity and figuring things out without a manualA clear communicator — you can hold your own in a client conversation and explain technical ideas in plain termsPrior startup or technology experience (required) — you've worked at a startup or tech company, founded something, or built and shipped your own product. You know what it's like to move fast in an environment without a playbook.Currently enrolled in a college or university program Bonus PointsA portfolio of AI projects you've built — apps, agents, automations, prompts, anythingFamiliarity with no-code/low-code tools or prompt engineeringExperience in a client-facing, sales, or consulting setting The DetailsLocation: Los Angeles, CA — hybrid (mix of in-person and remote)Duration: SemesterCompensation: Discussed during the interview processGrowth: Strong interns will be considered for a full-time offer after the summer

jobs.description: Employer: Inner Peak Expires: 09/21/2026 Marketing Intern: B2B Growth & Digital PresenceInner Peak builds mental health support for students, and we sell it to K-12 districts and universities. The team is small. There is no marketing function yet, and that's why we are hiring you: you'd be building it next to our VP of Sales & Marketing, who you'd report to directly.Worth saying up front, we don't have a playbook to hand you. We're still writing it. Some of what you try is going to flop. That's ok. We are paying you to learn together with us. jobs.feedName: Mike Curb College of Arts, Media, & Communication
jobs.title: Growth Intern (Content / Social Media / Community) at Pinnie Health
jobs.description: Employer: Pinnie Health Expires: 09/24/2026 Pinnie Health | New York, NY | Part-Time / Internship About Pinnie HealthMillions of older adults in America are failed by healthcare every day. They get discharged from the hospital with no follow-up plan. They miss medications because nobody explained the instructions. They give up trying to fight a denied insurance claim. They don't know what they're entitled to, and there's nobody helping them figure it out. The system wasn't built for them, it was built around them.Pinnie Health exists to fix that. We're building the first AI-powered care advocacy platform that gives every older adult on Medicare a dedicated human advocate, backed by AI that handles the research, coordination, and follow-up, at zero cost to the patient. We launched three months ago, we've already enrolled over 100 patients, we're licensed in 46 states, and we're growing fast. This is early-stage, high-impact work at the intersection of healthcare and technology, and we're just getting started. The RoleWe're looking for someone who understands how to build a social media presence from nothing. Someone who's already grown accounts on Instagram, Facebook, or both, and can prove it. You'll be our first dedicated social media hire. The job is building Pinnie's organic presence across Instagram and Facebook from scratch: daily content using a mix of AI-generated visuals, static graphics, patient testimonials, short-form video, articles, community posts, and whatever formats you think will connect with our audience. You'll also help manage a UGC agency we're working with to produce creator content around elder care and Medicare. The people you'll be making content for are older adults navigating Medicare, dealing with denied claims, trying to find a doctor who actually listens. The audience is their families, their caregivers, and the patients themselves. There are 67 million people on Medicare in this country, and almost nobody is making good content for them. That's the opportunity. We're not handing you a content calendar and asking you to execute. We want someone entrepreneurial who will come in, take ownership, and treat this like their own brand. You'll work directly with both founders, you'll have budget to spend, and you'll have the freedom to move fast. If you prove you can grow it, this becomes a full-time role. What You'll DoBuild and run our Instagram and Facebook. Create and publish content daily across both platforms. Static posts, carousels, Reels, Stories, testimonials, AI-generated imagery, quote cards, articles, community discussion posts. You'll figure out what formats work on each platform and double down on what gets traction. Use AI tools to move fast. You're comfortable with tools like Midjourney, ChatGPT, Higgsfield, or whatever's new this week. You use them to produce more and better content, not as a crutch. Grow an organic community. Build a following of Medicare beneficiaries, their adult children, and caregivers who actually engage. We care about people who click through and sign up, not vanity follower counts. Figure out what content sparks conversation and sharing in this audience. Manage our UGC agency. We're working with a UGC agency to produce creator content. You'll be the point person: reviewing briefs, giving feedback on deliverables, making sure the output fits our brand and actually performs. Experiment constantly. Test hooks, formats, posting times, hashtag strategies, content series. Track what works. Kill what doesn't. Bring us ideas we haven't thought of. Why PinnieYou'll build a brand for a massive underserved audience. 67 million Medicare beneficiaries. Their adult children. Their caregivers. Nobody is making great social content for this population. You get to own that space. We'll give you real ownership. No approval chains, no brand police. If you have an idea, pitch it at standup and post it that afternoon. We're a small team that moves fast, and we'll back you if you show results. The content matters. This isn't promoting a lifestyle brand or selling SaaS. The stories you'll tell are about real people getting help they couldn't find anywhere else. Families find us through the content you'll create. It can turn into a career. This starts as a part-time role. If you grow the channels and prove you can own the function, we'll convert it to full-time. Who You AreYou've grown a social media account and can show the numbers. Yours, a brand's, a client's. We want to see the before and after.You think big and are entrepreneurial. We want to take big swings and build a massive brand to drive awareness about a service that matters. You post consistently. Not once a week. Daily or close to it. You understand that cadence is half the game.You're fluent in AI content tools. You already use them in your workflow and can show us what you've made with them.You have visual taste. Your feed doesn't look like a template dump. You know color, composition, and typography well enough to make things people want to share.You can write captions and short copy that sounds human, not like a brand account. No "we're thrilled to announce." Real voice.Based in or near NYC. Some in-person collaboration in our Tribeca office, but most of the work is remote. What You Don't NeedA marketing degreeAgency experienceA follower countWe care about what you can make, not what's on your resume. DetailsLocation: Remote (If in NYC, hybrid as needed in our Tribeca office)Hours: ~20 hrs/week, flexible scheduleCompensation: Hourly Paid Internship ($ based on experience)Duration: 3 months with potential to extend or convert How to Apply1. Please submit your resume on this job post.2. Please go to pinnie.com and spend some time understanding what we do and who we serve. Then email aashay@pinnie.com the following: a. An account you've grown. Include the handle and the numbers (where it started, where it is now, timeframe). b. A content plan. We're starting from zero on Instagram and Facebook. Pitch us 2-3 content series or recurring formats you'd launch in your first two weeks. Tell us why you think they'd work for this audience. c. One big idea. What would you do in the first 90 days to build a real community around Pinnie? We're not looking for a polished deck. A few paragraphs showing how you think is plenty. That's the whole application.

jobs.description: Employer: Nationwide - Property & Casualty Expires: 09/24/2026 Nationwide is a leader in the insurance and financial services industry in America. We are a Fortune 100 company with a mission to protect people, businesses and futures with extraordinary care. The Nationwide summer internship program is designed to empower you, allowing you to forge a strong foundation for your career. Typical Skills and Education: Pursuing a Bachelor’s degree in insurance, actuarial science, mathematics, risk management, economics, finance, accounting, business administration or related field preferred. Knowledge, Abilities and Skills: Strong word processing, spreadsheet and presentation software skills. Ability to analyze data, identify underlying issues, devise alternative solutions, select most appropriate action and follow through to completion. Strong verbal and written communication skills necessary to interact with internal and external contacts. Ability to organize and present detailed analysis, information and concepts. Ability to prioritize own work/time, learn quickly, initiative and drive action, and work independently. Other criteria, including leadership skills, competencies and experiences may take precedence. Values: Regularly and consistently demonstrates Nationwide Values. Nationwide does not participate in the Stem OPT Extension program. jobs.title: Sales Development Representative (SDR) — Paid Sales Internship at Andy Eaton State Farm
jobs.description: Employer: Andy Eaton State Farm Expires: 09/24/2026 The OpportunityWant to graduate with real sales experience already on your résumé?Andy Eaton State Farm is looking for a motivated college student to join our Lakewood office as a part-time Sales Development Representative (SDR). You'll receive hands-on training and build measurable experience in prospecting, lead qualification, professional communication, CRM systems, and sales performance—all while earning a guaranteed hourly wage plus performance incentives.We'll provide the leads, training, scripts, and systems. Your job is to move fast, make contact, start conversations, and create opportunities for our sales team.You won't be responsible for closing the insurance sale. Your primary objective is simple: connect with prospective customers and transfer interested, qualified prospects to our sales team.What You'll GainThis isn't just a part-time job. It's an opportunity to develop skills that translate directly into a career in sales and business.You'll gain hands-on experience in:Sales developmentProspecting and lead managementProfessional communicationOvercoming objectionsBuilding rapportWorking within a sales pipelineGoal setting and performance trackingInsurance and financial servicesFor students interested in sales, business, marketing, finance, communications, entrepreneurship, or financial services, this is an opportunity to start building your résumé while you're still in school.What You'll DoAs an SDR, you'll be on the front end of our sales process.Your responsibilities will include:Making high-volume outbound calls to leads provided by our officeWorking toward a goal of approximately 60–70 outbound calls per hourStarting friendly, professional conversations with prospective customersIdentifying prospects who are interested and available to speak with our sales teamWarm-transferring qualifying prospects directly to a sales team memberFollowing our scripts, systems, and lead follow-up processAccurately tracking calls, contacts, and transfersWorking toward individual activity and performance goalsNo cold prospecting or finding your own leads—we provide the leads for you.Who We're Looking ForWe're more interested in your drive than your résumé.You don't need previous insurance experience. You don't even need previous sales experience.We're looking for someone who is:Competitive – You like having a number to beat.Driven – You don't need someone constantly pushing you.Resilient – Rejection and unanswered calls don't slow you down.Fast-paced – You enjoy staying busy and moving quickly.Personable – You can make people comfortable and communicate naturally.Coachable – You're willing to learn, follow a process, and improve.Dependable – When you're scheduled to work, you're ready to perform.Goal-oriented – You like seeing measurable results from your effort.If you're ambitious and willing to work, we'll teach you the rest.CompensationWe believe strong performance should be rewarded.This position combines a guaranteed hourly wage with uncapped performance incentives.Base Pay: $15.16/hourPerformance Incentive: $12 for each qualifying successful lead transferThe better you perform, the more you can earn.Example Earnings0 qualifying transfers/hour: $15.16/hour1 qualifying transfer/hour: $27.16/hour2 qualifying transfers/hour: $39.16/hour3 qualifying transfers/hour: $51.16/hourThere is no predetermined cap on qualifying transfer incentives. Actual earnings will vary based on individual performance.A qualifying successful transfer occurs when you connect an eligible prospective customer with an available member of our sales team in accordance with our lead-transfer procedures. Complete qualification requirements will be provided during training and in our written incentive compensation policy.ScheduleApproximately 20 hours per weekPart-time positionIn-person at our Lakewood, Colorado officeScheduling flexibility may be available around college classes and other commitmentsSpecific working hours will be discussed during the interview processPotential Career PathFor high-performing team members who are interested in continuing in the insurance industry, this role may also provide a pathway toward becoming a licensed insurance professional and pursuing additional sales opportunities within our agency. No insurance experience or license is required to start. We'll teach you the SDR role first and give you an opportunity to demonstrate what you can do. For students interested in sales, business, marketing, finance, communications, entrepreneurship, insurance, or financial services, this is an opportunity to start building meaningful professional experience while you're still in school.Where This Could LeadStrong performance in the SDR role may open opportunities for additional responsibilities within our agency. For interns interested in building a career in insurance and financial services, there may also be a pathway toward becoming a licensed insurance professional and moving into a larger sales role.Think You Can Do It?This is a high-activity sales development role.If making 60–70 calls per hour sounds intimidating, this probably isn't the position for you.But if you're competitive, enjoy a challenge, and like the idea of earning more when you produce more, we'd like to meet you.Previous sales experience isn't required.Drive is.Apply today and tell us why you'd be a great addition to our team.

jobs.description: Employer: Alliance for American Manufacturing Expires: 09/25/2026 POSITION DESCRIPTION: Fall Communications Intern (paid) NARRATIVE: The Alliance for American Manufacturing (AAM) is a non-partisan public policy organization dedicated to rebuilding domestic manufacturing through legislative and grassroots advocacy. As a highly successful labor-management partnership, AAM sits at the center of a broad coalition focused on domestic manufacturing, labor, and international trade issues. We offer an exciting and dynamic work environment, providing interns with a valuable opportunity to engage with critical policy issues impacting American jobs, economic recovery, manufacturing, and trade.AAM is seeking a full-time Communications Intern to support the organization’s communications and administrative operations. The intern will split their time between these two areas, contributing to effective storytelling, public relations strategies, and organizational processes. This role offers a unique opportunity to enhance your skills in written communications, web and social media management, and strategic outreach.QUALIFICATIONS:The ideal candidate is a current undergraduate student who has not yet attained a bachelor’s degree with an interest in our policy issues, strong written communication skills, and experience with social media platforms, with an emphasis on short form video. Familiarity with manufacturing, trade, or labor issues is appreciated but not required. REPORTS TO:Designated supervisor on Communications teamWORK DUTIES MAY INCLUDE: Research and write posts for AAM blog; Monitor online conversation in AAM issue areas, including on social media and other platforms; Help drive online conversation using a variety of social networking platforms; Assist in updating and maintaining AAM’s supporter database;Assist in updating AAM’s Made in America directory;Assist communications team in pitching stories to news outlets and new media;Attend virtual Congressional hearings and other meetings; Conduct research for AAM publications and activities; Assist in organizing virtual events and outreach efforts; Monitor, triage, and respond to emails from public;Perform additional duties assigned by AAM staff. LOCATION: This is an in-person opportunity; however, this may change in accordance with federal, state, or local safety guidelines or restrictions. Interns will be expected to work at least 4 full days in person at AAM’s Washington, DC office, with the remainder of the week worked remotely. To work remotely, the intern must confirm that he/she/they has full access to a secure computer with high-speed internet access.INTERN SESSION: Our fall session begins on or around Tuesday, September 8, 2026, and concludes on or around Friday, December 11, 2026. OTHER INFORMATION: This position is full-time (35 hours per week) but has flexibility for adjustment depending on the intern’s school schedule. jobs.feedName: Mike Curb College of Arts, Media, & Communication
jobs.title: Powell Museum Studies Internship at City of Naperville
jobs.description: Employer: City of Naperville - Naper Settlement Expires: 09/27/2026 The John K. and Judith H. Powell Museum Studies Internship Internship Summary: The Powell Museum Studies Intern will gain hands on collection management experience in an accredited museum setting. Guided by the museum’s Director of Collections and Registrar, the intern will learn about cataloging standards, controlled vocabularies, artifact enclosures, acquisitions procedures, and object handling through completion of a collection project. The project will be developed based on the intern’s interest and experience. Sample projects may include: Describing, tagging, and rehousing a collection of costume materials Conducting inventories of broadsides and works on paper and creating catalog records. Identifying artifacts for further processing, rehousing, and marking Assessing, tagging, and rolling textiles, updating catalog records accordingly Enhance catalog searchability by researching and adding subject headings Skills, Knowledge and Abilities: Reverence for artifacts, appreciation for history, and acute attention to detail are necessary. Strong verbal and written communication skills are important. Ability to work independently on projects and as an effective team member is required. Specific goals and expectations (tangible project results): Learn and implement basic object handling principles Understand broadly the concepts of content standards, controlled vocabularies, procedural standards, and authority records. Develop a working knowledge of collections management principles and terminology Learn to assess object condition and storage and care needs. Develop a working knowledge of collections documentation, including acquisition proposals, condition reports, deeds of gift, and authority files. Develop mechanical skills required in collections management, including marking objects and fabricating boxes, padded hangers, and archival weights. The John K. and Judith H. Powell Museum Studies Internship was established in 2012 and offers a $1000 stipend to the recipient for a term of 90 days. The late Jack Powell was chairman of the Naperville Heritage Society from 1980-1982 and Judy Powell was a member of the Weed Ladies floral design volunteers. This is the fourth year the internship has been awarded. This internship is open to undergraduate students. 2026 Term: 2 days a week from October 1st – December 30th onsite at Naper Settlement. About Naper Settlement and the Naperville Heritage Society Naper Settlement is a nationally accredited, award-winning outdoor museum set on 12 acres in the heart of Naperville at 523 S. Webster St., where history comes to play and the community comes to connect. With a commitment to the community and a focus to the future, the mission of the Naperville Heritage Society, administrator of Naper Settlement, is to collect, document, preserve and support the history of Naperville, Illinois, past and present. To learn more, please visit www.napersettlement.org.

jobs.title: Project Management Intern at Aldridge
jobs.description: Employer: Aldridge Expires: 09/27/2026 What we are looking for:Aldridge is seeking a Project Management Intern to join our dynamic and energetic team. This role will assist project management with administrative and operational duties that support project planning, execution, and closure.What you’ll do:Duties and responsibilities including:Assisting in coordinating the project team as directed by the teamPromoting safety on the jobsite, and working closely with the Safety Department to ensure that any safety issues are addressed properlyAdvocating the corporate quality program and assisting with the tracking and administrative aspects of our quality program components, including pre-job planning templates, task lists, and roles and responsibilitiesSupporting excellence in project execution through a multitude of tasks, including procuring tools, ordering and tracking material, documenting project costs, and interfacing with subcontractors and customersLearning and demonstrating our core competencies including adaptability/flexibility, customer focus, decision making/judgment, initiative, and qualityWho you are:We are pursuing students with the following qualifications:Demonstrate genuine interest in the construction industrySolution oriented, problem solver with a hands on and team oriented attitudeAbility to relate to a diverse group of individuals throughout the organizationCumulative GPA of 3.0 or above preferredWho we are:Aldridge, a family owned company, is one of the largest specialty contractors in the US, dealing in the power, transportation, and mission critical markets. jobs.title: Project Engineer Intern at Murray Company
jobs.description: Employer: Murray Company Expires: 09/27/2026 Come grow with us...At Murray Company, how we operate is defined by shared values that are 100 years in the making - Safety, Quality, Honesty, Hard Work and Pride of Ownership. These values have led to our company consistently being in the top 15% on ENRs Best Specialty Contractor’s list. Bring your enthusiasm and unique perspective to Murray Company where you will have the opportunity to grow with us professionally, personally, and financially. Join a team that cares about helping you thrive and succeed. You'll work alongside talented colleagues while establishing lifelong friendships and making a difference in our company and the specialty contracting community. Position SummaryAre you a current student looking to expand your knowledge and business acumen with practical hands-on experience and training opportunities? Start your career with a summer internship at Murray Company, - one of the nation’s Top 20 Mechanical Contractors and a leader in innovation and excellence. As an intern in our Operations group reporting to our talented project managers, you will work alongside our top-notch teams in our pre-construction, fabrication and field installation functions. This internship offers the opportunity to gain hands-on Project Management experience in support of mechanical projects of various sizes and specialties (plumbing, HVAC, process piping, and industrial). Location: Las Vegas, NV, with anticipated travel to designated project sites in and around the Las Vegas metropolitan areas. Compensation: $24.00 per hour Internship Program Schedule & HoursDuration: 40 hours per week for 10-12 consecutive weeks, beginning as early as May 2027.Typical working hours are Monday to Friday, 7 am - 4 pm (subject to change depending on local project requirements).Program participants must be available to work within the required schedule for the duration of the internship. Key ResponsibilitiesAssist in planning, scheduling, and coordinating mechanical projects.Provide support for reviewing designs, drawings, and specifications.Assist with managing project documentation, including submittals, RFIs, change orders, and reports.Participate in site visits to monitor progress and ensure compliance with specifications.Support the preparation of cost estimates and budgets.Aid in the implementation of quality control measures.Facilitate communication among project teams, subcontractors, suppliers, and clients.Assist with safety protocol implementation and compliance. QualificationsRequiredMust be currently enrolled in an accredited university program and actively pursuing a degree in Construction Management, Mechanical Engineering or related field.Proficiency in computer programs such as Microsoft Office Products (Excel, PowerPoint, Word, Outlook, etc.).Demonstrated ability to take initiative and interact effectively in a team environment.Availability to work 40 hours per week within the required schedule for the duration of the internship (typically 10 weeks).PreferredStrong organizational skills.Ability to multi-task and work in a fast-paced environment.Experience with construction software such as Revit, Navisworks, Bluebeam, Procore, ACC Build or other related programs. Physical RequirementsProlonged periods of sitting at a desk.Must be able to lift to 15 pounds at times.Must have sufficient visual acuity to view and interpret detailed construction drawings on computer screens and on paper.Must be able to traverse uneven surfaces on project sites and climb stairs to access project site temporary offices. Contingent EmploymentOffers of employment are contingent upon successful completion of the Company’s required pre-employment drug screening process. Murray Company is a federal contractor and complies with all applicable federal laws and regulations regarding controlled substances. Work AuthorizationMurray Company is not sponsoring employment-based visas at this time. Applicants must be currently authorized to work in the United States on an ongoing, permanent basis without the need for current or future visa sponsorship.

jobs.title: Field Intern at Dr. Kim Schrier's Congressional Campaign
jobs.description: Employer: Dr. Kim Schrier's Congressional Campaign Expires: 09/27/2026 Dr. Kim Schrier for Congress seeks a Field Intern for the 2026 election. The Field Intern will be responsible for supporting canvassing efforts in the 8th Congressional District and attending events with the Congresswoman and will play a critical role in community outreach. This position requires 12-15 hours a week, primarily in the evenings and weekends for voter contact. A regular week may include direct voter contact during weekday evenings and attending a parade or canvass launch on weekend mornings. The desired start date is September 15th, 2026 and an end date of November 3rd, 2026. The position pays $17.13 per hour with mileage reimbursement. The person in this position will be expected to work irregular hours, including evenings and weekends, and must have access to a laptop, internet, and a reliable car. The Field Intern will report to the Field Organizer. Job ResponsibilitiesWorking alongside the Field Organizer, volunteers, and other supporters on direct voter contact efforts including: phone banking, canvassing, text banking, and paradesCoordinating regular direct voter contact activities Coordinating yard sign distributionMeeting personal goals for phone calls, door knocking, and yard signs — averaging 200-250 doors knocked per weekRepresenting the campaign at events throughout the districtOther duties as assigned Skills and ExperienceSelf-motivated and self-startingAble to perform and thrive in high stress environmentsAble to prioritize multiple deadlines and handle regular challenges with a positive attitudeAble to work inclusively and collaborativelyExcellent written and verbal communication skills and an ability to communicate proactivelyAble to manage projects independently Job LocationThe position will be based in Issaquah, WA with travel throughout the 10,000 square mile district expected! To ApplyDo not apply through the Handshake platform. Please send a resume to info@drkimschrier.com with the subject line “Field Intern Application.” The position will remain open until filled. The start date for this position will be September 15th. Dr. Kim Schrier for Congress provides equal employment opportunities (EEO) to all employees and applicants for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, or genetics.

jobs.description: Employer: WSAW-TV Expires: 09/28/2026 The Training Program: Are you tired of just watching from the sidelines? Ready to stop "shadowing" and start actually doing the work that reaches thousands of people every single day? We’re looking for the next generation of media powerhouses, producers, reporters, weather experts, and sales executives who are hungry to dive head-first into the fast-paced world of local media. Communication skills: You can tell a story, pitch an idea, or explain a forecast with clarity and confidence.Reliability: You’re ready to commit to the full 10-week program and the 25-hour weekly schedule. Passion for local: You care about the community and want to see how local media makes a real difference.Why You’ll Love It Here:Real-world experience: You’ll graduate with more than just a line on your resume; you’ll have the experience of having done the job.Unprecedented access: With 113 stations across the U.S., you’re part of a massive, innovative network that’s leading the future of media.Career fast-track: We love hiring our own. This program is designed to be the ultimate audition for your first full-time role with Gray.Paid training: Earn while you learn. This is a paid internship.A culture of innovation: We’re evolving on purpose, and you’ll be right there on the front lines of that evolution.Qualifications/Requirements: • Be currently enrolled in a college/university, preferably in your senior year. • Available to work at least three shifts per week, up to 28 hours total, including nights and weekends • Strong work ethic and organizational skills. • Valid driver’s license with a clean driving record. jobs.feedName: Mike Curb College of Arts, Media, & Communication
jobs.title: Administrative Assistant at Camp Carl
jobs.description: Employer: Camp Carl Expires: 10/01/2026 We are looking for applicants ages 16-24 who are Christ-Centered, Relationally Focused, and Incredibly Fun! All our staff come ready for a life-changing summer where they are challenged in new ways, growing spiritually, and investing in campers for the sake of the Gospel.The role of the Administrative Assistant is to interact with customers (families and parents) to address their concerns, answer their questions, and assist them with their needs. The Administrative Assistant is a key part of our ministry. Our vision is to create an experience that exceeds the expectations of all our campers, summer staff, and families so that the love of Jesus can shine through us and is not dampened by a negative experience. Our focus is to create an environment that nurtures and encourages relationships with God and others. Things like daily camper mail, registration, office needs, phone calls, and more need excellent staff to make sure camp runs smoothly each week. We are looking for attentive people with a love for customer service.A Great Opportunity for Business & Communications Majors – This position is a great fit for college students studying business, communications, marketing, public relations, or a related field who want to gain valuable professional experience while spending their summer at camp. You’ll develop real-world skills in customer service, communication, organization, problem-solving, administration, and working with families - all while being part of a Christ-centered camp community. It’s an opportunity to build your resume, grow your professional skills, and have a meaningful summer investing in others.College Credit & Internships - It is possible to work at camp AND receive college credit. If you have an applicable field of study and would like to make your summer position into an internship, contact us once you apply, and we can discuss the possibility of an internship.Camp Carl's summer is broken into 4-week Terms. Summer Staff can choose to work either 4, 5, or 9 weeks by selecting the term(s) they wish to work. If you choose to work 9 weeks, you will be entitled to one week of unpaid vacation.Head to our website to apply: https://www.campcarl.life/joinourstaffPlease Note:Camp Carl is a non-denominational, evangelical Christian camp. As such, we require all employees to share our common faith and affirm our doctrinal statement. Employees must also agree to the standards outlined in our employee handbook regarding morality and lifestyle so that we are aligned in beliefs and values.

jobs.description: Employer: Camp Winadu Expires: 10/01/2026 Spend your summer in the beautiful Berkshire Mountains! jobs.description: Employer: Camp Bear Creek Expires: 10/02/2026 Media Specialist – Summer StaffLocation: Camp Bear Creek – Eastern IowaWebsite: https://bearcreek.camp/current-job-openings/summer-camp/Dates: May 23-July 24, 2027Camp Bear Creek is a Christian summer camp in Eastern Iowa serving kids from kindergarten through 12th grade. We’re looking for passionate, fun, dedicated people who want to spend a summer making a real difference — in the lives of campers and in their own.Come work as a Media Specialist at Camp Bear Creek. We are seeking a talented individual who is ready to put their skills into practice. The Media Specialist for the summer gains a lot of experience in, well, all things media. However, you also have the chance to do a lot more than that. You'll be immersed in the summer camp environment, interacting with children and youth in a Christian setting, learning how to capture their stories and how to share the mission of the camp, the joy of the moment, and the magic of summer in something as simple as a photograph or as complex as a ten minute video.The Media Specialist is responsible for camp photography and videography. You'll be out there with the camera, whether it's a DSLR or the GoPro, capturing that kid's giant smile as they go flying down the slip 'n slide or the moment they make it to the top of the rock wall or their splash landing at the bottom of the mud slide. The Media Specialist maintains the daily summer camp blog, which parents depend on as one of their only sources of communication with their child while they're away for six days at camp. They want to know what it feels like to be at camp even when they can't be there themselves, and the best Media Specialist will be able to help them do that. The Media Specialist updates the camp social media accounts, engaging a diverse community of all ages and experiences that spans back over a 65 year history. The Media Specialist designs a weekly summary video, compiling everything that they have captured during the week and uniquely putting it all together into an 8-10 minute video that parents and campers will not only watch over and over, but they'll want to show others because it so perfectly captures what camp was like.If you think you're ready for a summer like this and to be the Media Specialist, please complete the application through the camp’s website at https://bearcreek.camp/current-job-openings/summer-camp/ You'll walk away from the summer with a bigger portfolio, college credit, and a wealth of experience. Plus, you can't discount the chance to have some fun at camp, either!
